lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: What is the primary goal of the IoT implementation discussed in this lecture?
back: To integrate a DHT sensor with Raspberry Pi and include networking components for remote data logging using a client-server model.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: What networking model is used for data transmission between Raspberry Pi and the remote desktop?
back: A client-server model using UDP (User Datagram Protocol) based sockets.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: What is the basic aim of the Internet of Things regarding devices?
back: To create an interactive environment of networked devices, where more devices lead to a more intelligent and interactive system, maintaining performance.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: Describe the system overview for the remote data logging demonstration.
back: A network of temperature and humidity sensors will be connected to Raspberry Pi, data from the sensors are read, sent to the server over the network, and the data is saved in the server.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: List the essential hardware requirements for this IoT implementation.
back: A Raspberry Pi, a DHT sensor, a 4.7 kOhm resistor, and jumper wires.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: What is the purpose of the 4.7 kOhm resistor in the DHT sensor setup with Raspberry Pi?
back: It must be connected between the VCC and the data pin (pin one and two) of the DHT sensor.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: Identify the function of the second pin of the DHT sensor when viewed from left to right with the grid side up.
back: The second pin is used for transmitting data.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: To which Raspberry Pi pin is the VCC pin of the DHT sensor connected?
back: The 3.3 volt pin of the Raspberry Pi.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: Which Raspberry Pi pin (in BCM mode) is connected to the data pin (pin 2) of the DHT sensor?
back: Pin 11 of the Raspberry Pi.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: To which Raspberry Pi pin is the ground pin (pin 4) of the DHT sensor connected?
back: The ground pin of the Raspberry Pi.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: What GPIO mode must be used for the DHT sensor connection in this setup?
back: The board configuration for this DHT sensor must be in BCM mode, not in board mode.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: Which Python library is used to integrate the DHT22 sensor with Raspberry Pi?
back: The Adafruit_DHT library, provided by Adafruit which supplies the DHT22 sensor.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: What specific function from the Adafruit_DHT library is used to read data from the sensor?
back: The `adafruit_dht.read_retry` function.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: What is the general purpose of sockets in network communication?
back: Sockets generally create a two-way communication between two nodes in a network, one node termed as the server and the other as the client.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: What Python function is used to create a socket?
back: The `socket.socket` function.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: Name the three arguments of the `socket.socket()` function.
back: Socket family, socket type, and protocol (which is by default zero).

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: Which socket family is typically used for general-purpose internet protocols?
back: `AF_INET` (Internet protocols).

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: Which socket type is used for UDP-based communication (datagrams)?
back: `SOCK_DGRAM` (socket datagram).

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: What is a critical requirement for the server's IP address in a client-server model?
back: It is important that your server retain a singular IP address.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: What information must each client be aware of to connect to the server?
back: Each and every client should be aware of the server's IP address as well as the port to which the client is going to connect.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: What function is used by the server to associate its socket with a specific host and port?
back: The server binds to the port by calling the host name as the first argument and the port number as the second argument.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: After binding, what function does a server call to wait for client connections?
back: The server starts its listening function which waits for a client to connect to it.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: What does the `accept()` function return when a client connects to the server?
back: While a client has accepted the connection and connected to your server on that particular port, it will generate one address.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: What function does the client use to establish a connection to the server's IP address and port?
back: The client uses `s.connect()` to connect to that particular IP address of that server on that particular port.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: In the UDP client code, which function is used to send data to the server address?
back: The data is transmitted over the socket to that particular server address using `sendto()`.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: In the UDP server code, which function is used to receive data and the sender's address?
back: The data and address will be received from the socket using `recvfrom()`.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: In what mode should the `data_log.txt` file be opened on the server to prevent overwriting previous data?
back: The file should be opened in append mode so that your data keeps on appending onto the same file again and again without overwriting the previous data.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: How is the humidity and temperature data formatted when sent from the client to the server?
back: The humidity and temperature data are formatted in the terms of a string (e.g., '74.3,25.7').

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: What happens if the `data_log.txt` file does not exist when the server starts receiving data?
back: The server automatically creates another `data_log.txt` file.

lectureTitle: Lecture 31 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- II
front: Can multiple Raspberry Pis with sensors send data to a single server in this setup?
back: Yes, you can obviously include multiple Raspberry Pis and multiple sensors all sending data to this particular server or a single IP at the port.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: What is the primary focus of this lecture (Part III) regarding IoT implementation with Raspberry Pi?
back: Focusing more on the server side, that is once the data has arrived what exactly can be done with the data.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: What is the overall goal of the system discussed in these lectures?
back: Creating an interactive environment using a network of connected devices and remote data logging.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: What are the two main processing locations for data in the described IoT system?
back: The data may be processed on the client side as well as it may be processed on the server side itself.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: What is the initial step in the system overview for this demonstration?
back: Start off with a network of temperature and humidity sensors connected with Raspberry Pi board.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: What is the pin configuration for connecting the DHT sensor to the Raspberry Pi for power and ground?
back: DHT Pin 1 is connected to power, DHT Pin 4 to ground.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: Which Raspberry Pi pin is connected to the data pin (Pin 2) of the DHT sensor?
back: Pin 2 of DHT is connected to Pin 11 of the Raspberry Pi.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: What Python library is used for interfacing with the DHT sensor?
back: The Adafruit Python library for this DHT sensor.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: What is the role of the `iotsr.py` file in the client-server architecture?
back: This `iotsr.py` file is kept on the Raspberry Pi and when you remotely run this file it will generate a temperature and humidity value.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: In the client-server architecture, which device acts as the client and which acts as the server?
back: We create a client server architecture and establish connection between one client device and a desktop which acts as the server device.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: Where is the data received from the client stored on the server?
back: Successive data will be incoming into the server and get stored into a log file.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: Why is data processing (splitting, filtering) necessary when dealing with data from multiple sensors?
back: There may be chances of data corruption, incomplete data, server not able to receive the whole data, or data may not be properly formatted.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: What is the purpose of filtering data?
back: You need to filter the data to create a seamless and well structured database.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: Why is data splitting important if you have multiple sensors connected to a single node?
back: If we need to access individual data, suppose you only need to access the temperature value from multiple sensor readings.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: What common file format is used for saving data from the client where values are separated by a comma?
back: This is called a CSV or comma separated value file.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: What is the basic inbuilt Python function used to split a string into multiple strings based on a separator?
back: We will be using this basic inbuilt function of Python called split.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: How would you split the string 'sunday,monday,tuesday' using the comma as a delimiter in Python?
back: When we call this `data.split` function and we specify the delimiter in the arguments, you will see the result will be individual substrings.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: If you use `data.split('4')` on the string '123432454abc4rt', what would be the resulting substrings?
back: You have one two three then you have three two then you have five then abc then a blank since it has two fours so it includes a blank and then rt.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: What powerful library is supported by both Python and MATLAB for data plotting?
back: Both of these support a very powerful library called matplotlib.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: How do you typically import the `pyplot` module from `matplotlib` in Python?
back: Import matplotlib.pyplot as maybe a variable (e.g., `plt`).

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: What are the basic `matplotlib` commands for plotting 2D data, labeling the x-axis, and showing the plot?
back: You write `plot x comma y`, `x lable` gives labels on the plot for the x axis, and `show` function shows the plot.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: Which `matplotlib` function is used to add a title to the entire plot?
back: `title` gives title to the whole plot.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: What `matplotlib` function enables or disables an access grid on the plot?
back: `grid` it enabled or disabled an access grid on the plot.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: Which `matplotlib` function is generally used for animations by enabling interactive plot mode?
back: `ion` is the interactive plot mode, this is generally used for animations.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: What is the purpose of the `coverage_plot` function on the server side?
back: It animatedly plots whatever data is incoming into the server over the socket.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: How is the `plotting function` (e.g., `coverage_plot`) called on the server side to handle incoming data?
back: This plotting function is being called again and again basically iteratively within this loop.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: After splitting the incoming data (e.g., 'h,t') on the server, which element typically represents humidity and which represents temperature?
back: After splitting, since the data was in a csv format, so after splitting the zeroth element becomes humidity and the first element is temperature.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: What `matplotlib` command is used within the `coverage_plot` function to prevent new windows from being created for each plot update?
back: You set the figure to similar number as number one otherwise it will keep on creating new windows every time it plots something new.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: What is the function of `fig.canvas.draw()` in the server-side plotting code?
back: `figure.canvas.draw` it redraws the image without overwriting the previous parts.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: What is a key benefit of designing the IoT architecture such that only server-side scripts need to be changed for new functionality?
back: This thing will help save you a lot of effort you don't need to individually code the clients.

lectureTitle: Lecture 32 : Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi- III
front: What happens to the data logging and plotting when the client program is manually stopped?
back: The client program has been stopped manually and this data logging stops.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What is the primary goal of Software Defined Networking (SDN)?
back: To transform or restructure the existing network infrastructure in an efficient manner.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What is a key limitation of current day networks regarding network view?
back: Each switch does not have a global view of the network as a whole.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: In traditional networks, what happens if a switch goes down and there is no centralized control?
back: Finding an alternate route becomes a difficult task, as there is no centralized entity that can take care of it.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What are the three layers typically run on each switch in a traditional network?
back: Hardware, Operating System (OS), and Applications.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What is the core idea of SDN to overcome traditional network limitations?
back: To separate the application and operating system from the hardware.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: When did the idea of Software Defined Network (SDN) originate?
back: In 2008, with the OpenFlow project.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What was the name of the clean slate security architecture proposed by Stanford in 2006, which aimed for centralized security policies?
back: SANE.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What is the primary separation in the SDN architecture?
back: Separation of the data plane from the control plane.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What concept makes the separation of data and control planes possible in SDN?
back: Network Function Virtualization (NFV).

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: Name the three different planes in the SDN architecture.
back: Data plane, control plane, and application plane.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What is the Northbound API in SDN?
back: The interface between the control plane and the application plane.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What is the Southbound API in SDN?
back: The interface between the forwarding (data plane) and the control plane.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: Which protocol currently supports the Southbound API in SDN?
back: The OpenFlow protocol.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What is one of the key attributes of SDN regarding control logic?
back: The control logic is defined in a centralized manner.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: List two main challenges when implementing SDN in any network.
back: The Rule Placement Problem and the Controller Placement Problem.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: In SDN, what replaces routing tables in switches?
back: Flow tables.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: Who defines the flow rules in SDN?
back: The centralized controller.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: Where are flow tables stored in SDN switches?
back: In Ternary Content Addressable Memory (TCAM).

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What are the characteristics of TCAM memory in SDN switches?
back: It is limited in size, very expensive, and allows for very fast processing.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What message does a switch send to the controller if no flow rule is present for a received request?
back: A 'Packet In' message.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What is the typical delay involved in placing a new rule in an SDN switch after a 'Packet In' message?
back: Three to five milliseconds.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What is one challenge related to defining rules in SDN to minimize communication with the controller?
back: How to define the rules so that less number of 'Packet In' messages are sent to the controller.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: Are the fields in an OpenFlow rule fixed or configurable?
back: The fields are fixed in a particular version of OpenFlow.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: Describe the 'Hard Time Out' mechanism for flow rules in SDN.
back: All rules are deleted from the switch at a particular hard time, which can be done by resetting the switch for example.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: Describe the 'Soft Time Out' mechanism for flow rules in SDN.
back: If no flow is received associated with a particular rule for a timeout interval of time, then this particular rule is deleted.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What is the fundamental difference between SDN and OpenFlow?
back: SDN is a technology or a concept, while OpenFlow is a protocol that is used to communicate between the data plane and control plane.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: Name two popular open-source software implementations for OpenFlow switches.
back: Indigo, LINC, Pantou, or Open vSwitch.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: How does SDN help in minimizing operational costs and delays?
back: Operation cost and delay that are caused due to link failure can be significantly minimized using SDN.

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What kind of memory is required for flow tables in SDN switches due to its speed?
back: Ternary Content Addressable Memory (TCAM).

lectureTitle: Lecture 33 : Software Defined Networking- Part- I
front: What is the role of the centralized controller in SDN regarding flow rules?
back: The controller basically takes care of defining the flow rules based on which the streams of packets that are coming to each of the switches are processed.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is the primary protocol used for the Southbound API communication in SDN?
back: OpenFlow protocol.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is the purpose of the Northbound API in SDN?
back: To communicate between the control layer and the application layer.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is the 'east westbound API' concept in SDN?
back: This terminology comes into picture when we are talking about not a single controller but multiple controllers in the control layer.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is the main function of controllers in SDN regarding flow rules?
back: Controllers define the flow rule according to the application specific requirements.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is the typical delay for rule placement in a switch's flow table if not already existing?
back: About three to five milliseconds.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: Why is minimizing rule placement delay important in SDN?
back: Otherwise, there will be a huge control overhead and control-linked delay.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: Approximately how many requests can a single-threaded SDN controller handle per second?
back: Roughly about 200 requests in a second.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: Describe the logical connection between an SDN controller and switches.
back: The controllers are logically connected to the switches in a one-hop distance, though physically they can be multiple hops away.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is the basic characteristic of a 'flat architecture' for controller placement?
back: The switch and the controller are just logically one hop away. The switch sends a 'packet in' message to the controller if it doesn't have the flow rule.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: How does a 'hierarchical or tree architecture' arrange SDN controllers?
back: Controllers are placed hierarchically and connected to different switches in a tree-like fashion.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is a key characteristic of the 'ring architecture' for SDN controller placement?
back: Controllers are placed in a ring-like fashion, but a particular switch is connected to only one controller in this version.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is the primary benefit of using a 'mesh architecture' for SDN controller placement?
back: It increases reliability and improves the fault tolerance of the network.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: Differentiate between 'distributed' and 'centralized' control decisions in SDN.
back: Distributed: Each sub-network is controlled by a different controller. Centralized: A network is controlled by a single controller.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is the role of a 'backup controller' in SDN?
back: If the primary controller is down, the backup controller takes over, having a replica of the main controller to ensure uninterrupted network management.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: How can SDN enhance network security?
back: One can have enhanced level of security in the network by taking help of firewall, proxy, HTTP, and IDS.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is the difference between a simulator and an emulator for SDN experimentation?
back: Simulators simulate the entire thing (packet flows, network, nodes). Emulators can be connected to the real network where real traffic can flow through.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: Name a popular software used to create virtual networks with OpenFlow-enabled switches for SDN experimentation.
back: Mininet.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: Which programming language does Mininet run on?
back: Python.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: Name two popular controller configuration software used in SDN.
back: OpenDaylight and ONOS (also POX, NOX, Floodlight).

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is the core motivation behind SDN?
back: To separate out the control logic from the data logic (data plane) to make the network efficient.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is a significant trade-off or challenge in SDN regarding control messages?
back: More number of control packets are going to flow through the network, increasing control message overhead.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What two particular issues does the performance of SDN primarily depend on?
back: The rule placement and the controller placement in the network.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is the goal of 'unified network management' in SDN?
back: To have an unified network management architectural framework using SDN while leveraging the global view of the network.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is the next topic to be discussed after this lecture on SDN?
back: How SDN can be used in IoT to make the Internet of Things efficient.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is the role of the control plane in SDN?
back: The control logic is separated out to the control plane, which knows what has to be done with a particular flow and controls the overall flow in the network.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What does a switch do when it receives a packet for which it doesn't have a flow rule?
back: It will send a 'packet in' message to the controller.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is the main limitation of TCAM memory in the context of rule placement?
back: TCAM memory has limitations, which is a trade-off with delay in rule placement.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What kind of applications are now possible for SDN controllers beyond single-threaded ones?
back: Multi-threaded applications.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: In the context of SDN security, what is 'policy enforcement'?
back: Implementing a sequence of flow instructions for a policy chain, such as firewall, IDS, and proxy, to control traffic.

lectureTitle: Lecture 34 : Software Defined Networking- Part- II
front: What is the primary difference between a remote controller and a local controller in SDN experimentation?
back: A remote controller can be situated in a remote place and communicated using IP address and port number, while a local controller is situated locally.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What is one fundamental problem solved by integrating SDN into IoT?
back: Intelligent routing decision making.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: How does SDN simplify information handling in IoT?
back: It simplifies information collection, analysis, and decision making.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What aspect of network management is improved by SDN in IoT?
back: Visibility of network resources and simplified network management based on user/application requirements.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What kind of analysis and decision-making is enhanced by SDN in IoT?
back: Intelligent traffic pattern analysis and coordinated decisions through the controller.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What is the overall impact of SDN on IoT network intelligence and efficiency?
back: More intelligence is infused into the network, improving its efficiency.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: Name two tiers in the tiered segmentation of IoT networks.
back: Context-aware tier, Network tier, Application tier.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What is a key challenge in programming traditional sensor nodes?
back: Real-time programming of each sensor node is typically not feasible.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: Describe a characteristic of sensor node architectures from different vendors.
back: They follow vendor-specific architectures, lacking a single standard.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: Why are heavy computations difficult to perform at traditional sensor nodes?
back: Sensor nodes are resource-constrained.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What limitation does limited memory impose on traditional sensor networks?
back: Cannot insert too many control programs.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What is the role of the SDN controller in an integrated IoT network?
back: It controls different aspects, improves orchestration, and enhances service logic.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: How does SDN enable control over IoT end devices like sensors and actuators?
back: It provides centralized control.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What is the purpose of rule placement in an SDN-integrated IoT network, especially for access devices?
back: To handle issues like mobility and heterogeneity of end devices.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: Where is traffic engineering typically managed in an SDN-integrated IoT network?
back: At the transport network level.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What functions are handled at the data center networks in an SDN-integrated IoT setup?
back: Flow classification and enhanced security.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What is the name of the protocol proposed by Low et al. in 2012 for sensor networks?
back: Sensor OpenFlow protocol.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: Name the two ways Sensor OpenFlow protocol handles data forwarding.
back: Value-centric data forwarding and ID-centric data forwarding.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: Explain value-centric data forwarding in Sensor OpenFlow.
back: Data is forwarded if the sensor data exceeds a certain threshold value.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: Explain ID-centric data forwarding in Sensor OpenFlow.
back: Data is forwarded based on the ID of the source node.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What is a limitation of the Sensor OpenFlow protocol mentioned in the lecture?
back: Real-life implementation of such a method is not yet available.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What is the name of the protocol proposed by Bera et al. in 2016?
back: Soft WSN protocol.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: Name two major component solutions of the Soft WSN protocol.
back: Sensor device management and topology management.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What does sensor device management in Soft WSN comprise?
back: Sensor management, delay management, and active sleep management.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: How did Soft WSN compare to traditional WSN in terms of packet delivery ratio?
back: It showed much improved packet delivery ratio.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: How did Soft WSN affect the number of replicated data packets compared to traditional WSN?
back: It reduced the number of replicated data packets.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: Why does Soft WSN have a higher number of control packets in the network?
back: Each time a node receives a new packet, it asks the controller for adequate forwarding logic.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What is the name of the SDN-integrated WSN platform published in INFOCOM 2015?
back: SDN-WISE.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What key feature does SDN-WISE propose for rule placement at sensor nodes?
back: A flow table for rule placement is available at the sensor nodes.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: How can nodes be programmed in real-time in SDN-WISE?
back: Any programming language can be used through API to program the nodes in real time.

lectureTitle: Lecture 35 : Software Defined IoT Networking- Part- I
front: What protocol do sensor nodes typically run in the SDN-WISE work?
back: The 802.15.4 protocol.
